note: Recast from the description of the new species by Rocha & Cancello (2009), original in English; no measurement data.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other species of the genus by the combination of large compound eyes and small fontanelle; the most similar species are O. aduncus and O. wheeleri, from which it differs in the small fontanelle. The soldier head capsule is larger than in O. mirim and O. pilosus and smaller than in O. humilis, with a distinct weak constriction at the base of the lateral projections; the most similar species is O. aduncus, whose lateral projections are not constricted at the base.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes large, separated from the lower margin of the head by less than the greatest diameter of an ocellus. Ocelli kidney-shaped and large in dorsal view; oval in lateral view, separated from the compound eye by less than its least diameter. Fontanelle wide and small. Head capsule with short hairs and scattered setae. Labral setae arranged in two rows. Pronotum with fairly dense short hairs and setae; mesonotum and metanotum with short hairs, concentrated on the centre and the posterior margin. Head dark brown to brown, pronotum and tergites brown to pale brown, sternites pale yellow, legs pale brown, wing scales brown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head parallel in dorsal view, the lateral projections with a distinct weak constriction. Dorsal tubercle prominent in lateral view, situated behind the lateral projection. Mandibles type 1, with a tooth-like process at the middle. Head capsule with short hairs (denser ventrally) and scattered setae, minute hairs over the whole head capsule. Postmentum with setae. Pronotum with short hairs and setae, more numerous on the margins; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with setae; abdominal tergites densely setose, the sternites with short hairs and erect setae on the posterior margin.
